issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inverse exists only when Ψ has full column rank; merely having m≥s is insufficient. In the underdetermined experiments explicitly discussed later, Ψ*Ψ is necessarily singular. Least-squares minimizers nevertheless exist in that regime, contrary to the accompanying necessity claim. The displayed formula is therefore not a general Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse implementation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the genuine Moore–Penrose solution Ψ†b, specifying the minimum-norm selection when minimizers are nonunique. Restrict the displayed inverse formula and uniqueness claim to full-column-rank matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The supplied computational prescription does not define the least-squares approximations used in the underdetermined regime.
issues.title: The stated pseudoinverse implementation requires an unprovided rank condition
issues.why_classification: A standard rank-aware pseudoinverse implementation repairs the procedure without changing the approximation method or the formal full-rank recovery guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exist a compact set $\mathcal{K}\subset \mathbb{C}^d$, with $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathcal{K}$

issues.failure_explanation: Even after correcting the theorem's reversed containment, Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix does not require U⊂int(K). It permits K=U, whose complex interior is empty, or U together with a disjoint complex ball. Holomorphy on int(K) then imposes no analytic regularity along U. For a two-node graph with edge coefficient |y₂| and initial state (1,0), the first component is (1+exp(-2T|y₂|))/2, which has no holomorphic extension around U but satisfies that compact-only assumption.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require U⊂int(K), consistently in the theorem's containment condition and its extension hypothesis, rather than merely U⊂K.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem does not establish its advertised holomorphic extension under its general hypotheses. The approximation corollaries avoid this defect because they explicitly require a polyellipse inside int(K).
issues.title: Compact containment does not provide a holomorphic neighborhood of the parameter domain
issues.why_classification: An essential strengthening of the regularity hypothesis is needed, but it leaves the later polyellipse-based regimes and their rates intact and requires no new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, observe that we can reformulate problem \eqref{eq:ted} (where $\bm{C}$ is replaced by $\tilde{\bm{C}}$) as the following parametric Volterra integral equation:

issues.failure_explanation: The kernel repeatedly supplied to the Volterra lemma yields u(t)=u₀+M(t)∫₀ᵗu(s)ds, not the integral form of u′(t)=M(t)u(t). For example, when M(t)=tA and Au₀≠0, these equations have different quadratic terms at t=0. Thus the lemma is applied to the wrong constructed evolution, and Step 2 cannot infer the asserted ODE from that construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct the kernel as h(t,s,u,z)=M(s,z)u and verify the lemma for this kernel. The existing continuity, holomorphy, and uniform matrix-norm arguments then apply with the integration-time variable.
issues.overall_effect: The presented holomorphy argument does not cover the claimed nonautonomous diffusion equation, undermining the results that invoke that argument.
issues.title: The Volterra kernel represents a different time-dependent evolution
issues.why_classification: Correcting the integral construction and its time-variable checks is local and routine; it preserves the entire time-dependent regime and all stated rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The triangle-inequality estimate needs |Wᵢⱼ|, whereas the hypotheses permit arbitrary real weights. For a two-node edge of weight -1 and diffusion coefficient 1, the matrix row has ℓ¹ norm 2 while the displayed right-hand side is -2. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use absolute values of the edge weights throughout the row-norm estimate and take the supremum over [0,T]×K. Continuity and compactness already supplied in the source make this bound finite.
issues.overall_effect: The stated verification of the Volterra lemma's Lipschitz hypothesis fails for signed weighted graphs allowed by the source.
issues.title: The Lipschitz estimate incorrectly treats real edge weights as nonnegative
issues.why_classification: The corrected norm estimate is routine and preserves the full stated real-weight scope without changing any conclusion or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: Such a supremum need not be differentiable. Within the graph model, take a two-node edge coefficient c(t,z)=z(2t-1), initial state (1,-1), T>1, and H consisting of parameter values z=0 and z=1. The two squared norms are 2 and 2exp(-4(t²-t)); their supremum has a corner at t=1. The displayed classical derivative inequality and subsequent application of Gronwall therefore require an argument not given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Gronwall separately to the already established pointwise inequality v′(t,z)≤2‖M(t,z)‖v(t,z), and only afterward take the supremum and square root.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the explicit uniform bound B, and hence the estimates using that bound, has an invalid differentiation step.
issues.title: The supremum of the energy functions is differentiated without justification
issues.why_classification: The available pointwise estimate gives a routine bypass that preserves, and actually strengthens, the stated uniform bound.

issues.failure_explanation: No condition connects η to the observation noise or the polynomial truncation residual. Replacing the noise term by η cannot yield a bound for arbitrary noise. In the allowed constant-only approximation space, f=0 and constant noise a>η give the QCBP solution a-η, whereas B=0 and the asserted error bound depends only on η. Taking a arbitrarily large defeats that bound even after correcting its normalization. Truncation can also make the intended coefficient vector infeasible with zero observation noise.

issues.failure_explanation: The decoder's η bounds an already normalized residual, whereas ‖n‖₂ in Corollary cor:CS is the unnormalized sample-noise norm. diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $f: \mathcal{U} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ that admits a holomorphic extension to a Bernstein polyellipse $\mathcal{E}_{\bm{\rho}} \subset \mathbb{C}^d$.

issues.failure_explanation: Holomorphic extendability places no bound on amplitude, yet the approximation constant depends only on ρ and p. For the theorem's finite set S, choose ν∉S and f=Aψν with zero noise. This polynomial is entire, and every approximation in P_S has L² error at least |A|, while the claimed right-hand side is independent of A. The graph corollary inherits the same defect because diffusion solutions scale linearly with the unrestricted initial state.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the auxiliary theorem for a normalized analytic class and restore the factor ‖f‖_{L∞(Eρ)} when scaling back. In Corollary cor:LS, bound that factor by the available B(u₀,T,M).
issues.overall_effect: The least-squares error bounds are false for arbitrarily scaled analytic functions and graph initial conditions.
issues.title: The least-squares theorem gives an amplitude-independent bound for an unbounded function class
issues.why_classification: Essential amplitude dependence must be added, but the source supplies the necessary envelope and the algebraic exponent, sampling regime, and noise term can all be retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\varrho$ be either the uniform or Chebyschev measure on $\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d$

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficient calculation uses unweighted Lebesgue integrals, but Chebyshev polynomials are orthogonal under the Chebyshev measure. The Chebyshev quadratic is proportional to 2x²-1, whose Lebesgue integral is nonzero. Thus the displayed vanishing argument does not establish the claimed coefficient support in the Chebyshev case. The infinite tail must also be integrated against a normalized product probability measure, not the literal unnormalized product written here.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Perform the coefficient calculation with the corresponding normalized product measure and its one-dimensional marginals. Then every nonconstant tail factor has zero integral by the stated orthogonality.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix does not correctly establish the finite-dimensional reduction used for its two-measure least-squares guarantee.
issues.title: The finite-dimensional least-squares reduction uses the wrong orthogonality measure
issues.why_classification: Correcting the integration measures restores the same factorization argument and preserves both measure choices and all rates without an additional lemma.
